answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can demand that each new identity complete a slow verifiable delay puzzle whose solution produces a unique raven-like signature of computational effort. Only after this hollow process finishes can the agent participate, and every subsequent action must echo that initial cost through linked proofs. An attacker cloning thousands of identities must therefore expend real time and electricity for each one, far exceeding any short-term gain from fake votes or claims.
